$comment: CANONICAL generator stable-name manifest (ADR-0021 D3). The single cross-port source of truth for generator stable names. Every port's generator registry is conformance-tested against this file: (1) every generator a port exposes MUST use a name listed here; (2) for each generator, the `ports` array lists exactly the ports expected to expose it (presence is checked both ways); (3) because all ports validate against this one file, a shared concept (e.g. `routes`) is spelled identically everywhere. Port ids: typescript, csharp, java, kotlin, python, and rust (ADR-0065, held to the same four checks by its own test). `tier`: native (idiomatic per-port code) or neutral (language-neutral pages that describe the model the same way in every port; a description of the output, not a door: every generator runs when the project's generator list declares it, ADR-0034 Amendment 9). `layer`: one of model, persistence, service, api, client, docs, capability — the grouping an adopter SELECTS BY, gated in every port exactly as `tier` is (see README.md). `eject`: "full" (the owned copy holds the generator's emit) or an exemption with a written reason and the ruling that grants it; the top-level `eject` block carries the engine surface, the exempt non-generator emitters and the pending list (ADR-0034 Amendment 8, see README.md). Adding/renaming a generator = edit THIS file + the port registry together; the conformance gate fails otherwise.

entity.concept: Per-entity model/class — the entity module (table-backed or value object).

routes.concept: Per-entity REST endpoint surface (controllers / routes / router).

output-parser.concept: Per-template response parser: a strict parse that rejects a reply not matching the @responseRef shape, plus a tolerant lenient extract for a raw model reply, which reports per field instead of throwing on a bad reply.

render-helper.concept: Per-renderable-template render helper (typed render wrappers). BOTH template subtypes render (ADR-0052), so on csharp/java/kotlin/python/rust this covers template.output AND template.prompt; on typescript a prompt's render handle is the separate `prompt-render` generator instead, so typescript's render-helper is template.output only. Same stable name, one concept, one per-port split — stated here because the concept line is shared and the split is not.

extractor.concept: Per-template typed extract<Name> helper: tolerant recovery of the typed response from dirty model text; throws only when a @required field is lost.

template.concept: Generic Mustache template primitive (walk + template -> files).

eject.exempt: The Mustache primitive. The template and the walk the adopter supplies are its emit logic, so the package holds none to hand over.

prisma-schema.concept: A Prisma schema (schema.prisma) for the model's tables, with the CHECK constraints Prisma cannot declare in a companion SQL file.
prisma-schema.note: TYPESCRIPT ONLY by design (#479): Prisma is a TypeScript ORM, and the generator is a reference helper (ADR-0034 Amendment 3) writing a schema that imports nothing.

callable.concept: Per-entity callable wrapper for a callable source (storedProc / tableFunction); in TS it also covers the service surface wrapping the query helpers.

barrel.concept: Single index module re-exporting every generated entity module.

names.concept: Per-entity physical database name constants (table/view name, schema, column names).

rules-names.concept: Business-rules name constants (ADR-0067 layer 0): each lifecycle's states, initial and terminal states and transitions, the permission each derived command and each operation asks for, and the error codes. A layer generator: it acts on the rules vocabulary, so the codegen-noop rules corpus does not hold it. On rust they are closed enums in a `<package>_rules` crate, which also names each derived command and declared operation.

contract-types.concept: Contract types with no persistence mapping (ADR-0067 layer 1): each store-backed entity's read, create and update shapes, each projection's read shape, each declared operation's input, output and errors, and the wire error bodies. TypeScript writes the whole layer. C# so far writes each entity's create and update records, which leave out the server-owned members (generated key, @autoSet stamp, readOnly and derived fields, TPH discriminator) and tell an omitted member from an explicit null. On rust an entity's read, create and patch shapes are the entity generator's model crate, which carries no persistence mapping, and this generator writes a `<package>_contract` crate per package with a declared operation: each operation's input, output, business errors and error body, the read shape of a returned projection that is not a served read, and the wire error contract. The other ports add theirs with their rules-layer work.

service.concept: The service layer (ADR-0067 layer 4): one module per metadata package, a function per operation, and a factory that binds them to the dependencies passed in. Each store-backed entity gets its derived list, get, create, update and delete; every write runs in one transaction (a savepoint inside a caller's) with the declared write rules (ADR-0045). TypeScript, behind its own transport (`service-routes`), and Rust (over the `repository` store crates, its write running inside a caller's transaction through its `_in` twin); the other ports add theirs with their rules-layer work.

service-routes.concept: A thin REST transport over the service layer (ADR-0067 layer 5), one per metadata package: each route parses the request, calls one service operation and sends what it answered, and holds no rules. It answers the shared REST contract as `routes` does. TypeScript (Fastify) and Rust (axum, one router per package with an actor extractor; opt-in at `cargo meta init --transport`, because it brings a web framework into the build).

service-routes-hono.concept: The `service-routes` transport on Hono: the same routes over the service layer (ADR-0067 layer 5), mounted on a Hono app, answering the shared REST contract the same way. TYPESCRIPT ONLY by design, as `routes-hono` is: Hono is a TypeScript framework.

prompt-render.concept: Per-template.prompt render handle over the render engine, aggregated into one module. TYPESCRIPT ONLY by design: the other ports emit a prompt's render helper from `render-helper` (see its note) rather than a second generator.

api-docs.concept: Per-entity/template SDK API reference (generated-code API; human + agent forms).
api-docs.note: An ordinary generator, listed in the project's generator list and run by the gen command (ADR-0034 Amendment 9), in every port: `apiDocsFile()` in `generators` that `meta gen` runs (TypeScript), an `ApiDocsGenerator` entry in `codegen/Generators.cs` that `dotnet meta gen` runs (C#), `api-docs` in a target's `generators` that `metaobjects gen` runs (Python), or a `<generator>` entry that `mvn metaobjects:generate` runs (Java, Kotlin).

trace-helper.concept: Per-entity typed record<Entity>/call<Entity> trace helpers (extract + buildLlmCallRow + persist; LlmCallBase-derived entities only).
trace-helper.note: TS emits record<Entity> + call<Entity>; Java (codegen-spring) emits record<Entity> only — the Java LlmClient seam is BYO/vendor-neutral and not ported (ADR-0024). Python emits record_<entity> only (same BYO-caller rationale).

db-context.concept: Single EF Core DbContext binding every generated entity.

expression-indexes.concept: The expression (@expr) indexes the ORM model cannot carry, as one SQL file applied after the schema.

repository.concept: Per-entity repository seam (Java: Spring Data interface; Kotlin: an open Exposed persistence base with CRUD + patch bodies; Rust: a store crate per package over sqlx, with list, count, get, create, update, delete and the guarded lifecycle update).

value-object.concept: Per-value-object Spring record with jakarta constraints (the DTO/Patch bind target for a field.object jsonb column, and a template's payload/response type).

exposed-table.concept: Kotlin Exposed table object per table-backed or view-backed entity or projection, and per view-backed report.

spring-config.concept: Spring wiring/configuration for the generated surface.

shared-model.concept: FR-023: a publisher's flattened shared-model artifact + manifest for a consumer's `meta deps sync`.

form.concept: Per-entity React form component over the generated Zod schema.

hooks.concept: Per-entity TanStack Query hooks (useEntity / useEntities / useCreate / useUpdate / useDelete).

grid.concept: Per-entity TanStack Table column definitions, from a layout.dataGrid declaration.

grid-hook.concept: Per-entity server-driven grid state hook (sort/filter/page) over the generated columns.

client.concept: A typed HTTP client (reqwest) for the REST surface the other ports' `routes` generators serve.
client.note: RUST ONLY for now, by decision (ADR-0065). Another port adopting the name adds itself to `ports`.

commands.concept: clap command groups, one per metadata package, that call the generated `client`.
commands.note: RUST ONLY for now, by decision (ADR-0065), a deliberate difference from the other ports. Another port adopting the name adds itself to `ports`.

requirement-tests.concept: Per-requirement test stub, one per requirement.functional claim in the ledger.

report-export.concept: Per-report export module (CSV, JSON and XML writers over a served object.report's derived fields) plus one shared writer module per project; wires the ?format= branch into the report list routes. Standalone catalog generator, never implied by a library (ADR-0034 Amendment 5).

contract-schema.concept: JSON Schema 2020-12 for the model's wire shapes (read, create, update), and a strict structured-output profile. A different concept from json-schema, which describes metadata files.
contract-schema.note: TYPESCRIPT ONLY by design (ADR-0034 Amendment 10): a neutral artifact with one engine, so an adopter on any port runs it through the Node `meta` CLI, and the output depends on the model and the wire setting, never on the port.

openapi.concept: One OpenAPI 3.1 document for the generated REST surface, whose components are the contract-schema shapes.
openapi.note: TYPESCRIPT ONLY by design (ADR-0034 Amendment 10): every port's routes answer the same REST contract, so one engine states it for all of them.

cube-model.concept: Cube data model files (model/cubes/*.yml, model/views/*.yml) exported from the reporting vocabulary.
cube-model.note: TYPESCRIPT ONLY by design (FR-044 Plan 4, reporting design R6): a reference helper (ADR-0034 Amendment 3) writing YAML that imports nothing; no other port ships an exporter.

docs.concept: Neutral per-entity / per-template Markdown documentation pages.
docs.note: Listed like any generator; writes to the `docs` target (ADR-0034 Amendment 9).

requirements.concept: The requirement ledger as documentation: requirements.md for people and requirements.toon for tools.
requirements.note: Listed like any generator; writes to the `docs` target (ADR-0034 Amendment 9). A project that declares no requirement.* node gets no file.

agent-docs.concept: Pages written for a coding agent working in the project: the schema, the UI surface and the requirements.
agent-docs.note: Listed like any generator; writes to the `docs` target (ADR-0034 Amendment 9).

metamodel-docs.concept: The reference of the built-in metamodel: every type, subtype and attribute the build registers, by provider.
metamodel-docs.note: TYPESCRIPT ONLY: it was `meta docs --metamodel` until 1.1.0 (ADR-0034 Amendment 9).

docs-site.concept: The browsable HTML site of the model: navigation, search, a page per package and per object, ER diagrams.
docs-site.note: TYPESCRIPT ONLY: it was `meta docs --site` until 1.1.0 (ADR-0034 Amendment 9).

eject.exempt: The site builder is engine: it assembles the page data the site's templates read, and what an adopter changes is those templates and the assets beside them, which `meta eject docs-site` copies into codegen/docs-site/ and the generator reads from there.

plantuml.concept: PlantUML class diagram of the object model.

html-docs.concept: Single-page HTML reference of the registered metamodel types, read from the type registry.

ai-docs.concept: JSON reference of the registered metamodel types written for an AI reader, read from the type registry.

json-schema.concept: JSON Schema that validates metadata files, read from the type registry.

mustache.concept: The pre-`template` Mustache generator, kept so a pom that names its class keeps building.

eject.exempt: Deprecated in favour of `template` (ADR-0021 D4) and kept only so existing poms build. A deprecated generator is not handed over.

eject.$comment: The eject contract (ADR-0034 Amendment 8), asserted in every port by its eject-contract test. `engineSurface.<port>`: `codegenPackages` are the namespaces that hold generators and their emit code; `engine` lists the members of those namespaces an owned copy may still import (the generator base and runner, model questions, naming and type-mapping tables). Anything else inside `codegenPackages` writes output and must be handed over with the generator. Everything outside `codegenPackages` (loader, metamodel, runtime, render) is core and may be imported freely. `exemptEmitters`: code that writes into an adopter's repository but is not a generator, ruled out of eject with a reason. `pending`: every place the contract does not hold yet, by generator, port, assertion (census, completeness or depth) and gap number; a depth entry lists in `outside` the modules its owned copy still imports from outside the engine surface. A port's test fails when a pending entry passes, and when a gap appears that is not listed. 1.1.0 does not ship with a non-empty pending list: the release scripts and the publish workflows refuse a version with no prerelease suffix while eject.pending holds an entry (scripts/eject-release-gate.mjs).

exemptEmitters.name: docs-site builders
exemptEmitters.exempt: The builder is engine: what an adopter changes is the site's templates and assets, which `meta eject docs-site` copies into the project (codegen/docs-site/). The builders assemble the page data the templates read.
exemptEmitters.ruling: ADR-0034 Amendment 8, ruling 3, as Amendment 9 restates it

surface.$comment: The generator-authoring surface (ADR-0034 Amendment 12): the part of each port's codegen engine a team writes its own generator against, and the only part of the engine the compatibility policy promises. Four roles per port: `generator` (the interface a generator implements and what it is handed and returns, including the one declaration of what it provides), `modelWalk` (the questions about the loaded model a generator asks that are not a single metadata accessor), `writer` (what lays out emitted text) and `naming` (the spellings of metadata names in the port's language). Entries use the same spelling as `eject.engineSurface.<port>.engine`. The surface is versioned with the port's codegen package and changes under docs/compatibility-policy.md; every other engine member is internal: an owned copy may still import it (the eject contract), but it may change in any release. Modules that `meta eject` copies into the project (reference templates) are owned code and never surface. A role with an empty list says the port has no module in that role yet. Each port's T7 row pins the surface's exported names with a name-level snapshot test and checks that every entry is also an engine entry.
